'''William Loudon Mollison''' (19 September 1851 – 10 March 1929)<ref name="Dr. W. L. Mollison.">{ [[The Times]] (London, England), Monday, &nbsp;11 March 1929; pg. 21; Issue 45148.}</ref> was a Scottish mathematician and academic.<ref>{{Who's Who | title=Mollison, William Loudon | id = U214230 | type = was | volume = 1920–2016 | edition = April 2014 online | access-date = 18 November 2018 }}</ref> From 1915 to 1929, he was [[Master (college)|Master]] of [[Clare College, Cambridge]].<ref>[[Alumni Cantabrigienses]]: A Biographical List of All Known Students, Graduates and Holders of Office at the University of Cambridge, from the Earliest Times to 1900, [[John Venn]]/[[John Archibald Venn]] [[Cambridge University Press]] [https://archive.org/details/p2alumnicantabri04univuoft/page/434 > (10 volumes 1922 to 1953) Part II. 1752–1900 Vol. iv. Kahlenberg – Oyler, (1947) p434]</ref>

==Early life and education==
Mollison was born on 19 September 1851 in [[Aberdeen]], Scotland.<ref name="CAA">{{cite journal |last1=Knewstubb |first1=Peter |title=William Loudon Mollison (1851–1929) |journal=Clare Association Annual |year=2012 |pages=65–67 |url=https://www.clarealumni.com/file/documents/MU16632-Clare-Annual---Web.pdf |access-date=18 November 2018 }}</ref><ref name="Year Book">{{cite book |title=The New International Year Book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C4NMAAAAMAAJ |year=1930 |publisher=Dodd, Mead and Company |location=New York City, NY |page=581}}</ref> He was educated at [[Aberdeen Grammar School]], then an all-boys grammar school.<ref name="WWW">{{cite web |title=Mollison, William Loudon |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540891.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-214230 |website=[[Who Was Who]] |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=18 November 2018 |doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U214230 |date=1 December 2007}}</ref> He studied mathematics and [[natural philosophy]] at the [[University of Aberdeen]], graduating in 1872 with a [[first class honours|first class]] degree.<ref name="obit Aberdeen">{{cite news |title=Births, Deaths, Marriages and Obituaries – Master of Clare |work=Aberdeen Press and Journal |issue=23148 |date=12 March 1929 |page=11}}</ref> That year, he was awarded the Ferguson Scholarship by Aberdeen and matriculated into [[Clare College, Cambridge]] to continue his mathematical studies.<ref name="CAA" /><ref name="WWW" /> He became a Foundation Scholar in 1873.<ref name="CAA" /> His private tutor while at Cambridge was [[Edward Routh]].<ref name="Mercury">{{cite news |title=CAMBRIDGE UNIVERSITY – Mathematical Tripos |work=The Leeds Mercury |issue=11795 |date=29 January 1876}}</ref> He graduated from the University of Cambridge in 1876 as the [[Second Wrangler]].<ref name="CAA" /><ref name="Mercury" /><ref>{{cite book |last=Tanner |first=Joseph Robson|title=The historical register of the University of Cambridge, being a supplement to the Calendar with a record of University offices, honours and distinctions to the year 1910|url=https://archive.org/details/1910historicalreg00univuoft/page/300|format=PDF|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|access-date=18 November 2018|year=1917}}</ref>

==Career==
On 29 April 1876, Mollison was elected a [[Fellow (Oxbridge)|Fellow]] of [[Clare College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Scotchmen at Cambridge University |work=The Dundee Courier & Argus |issue=7103 |date=1 May 1876}}</ref> He was an examiner for the [[University of St Andrews]] between 1876 and 1880.<ref name="Year Book" /> He was a mathematics lecturer at [[Jesus College, Cambridge]] from 1877 to 1882, and at Clare College from 1882.<ref name="WWW" /> In addition to his college teaching, he was a private tutor or "coach" in mathematics.<ref name="CAA" />

Due to ill health, he moved from teaching a large number of students, privately and through his college, into administration.<ref name="CAA" /> He was appointed junior tutor of Clare College in 1880,<ref name="WWW" /> and was made its senior tutor in May 1894.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Tutorship of Clare |work=Cambridge Independent Press |issue=4065 |date=4 May 1894 |page=5}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[Council of the Senate]] of the University Of Cambridge in 1892,<ref name="CAA" /> and appointed Secretary of the General Board of Studies of the University in 1904: he stepped down from both these posts in 1920.<ref name="WWW" /> He served as ''[[locum tenens]]'' for the then Master (Edward Atkinson) from 1913 to 1915.<ref name="WWW" /> Mollison was unanimously elected as Atkinson successor as the 38th [[Master of Clare College, Cambridge]] in March 1915.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Master of Clare |work=Cambridge Independent Press |issue=5155 |date=2 April 1915 |page=5}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mollison was married to Ellen Mayhew.<ref name="WWW" /> They had one son and two daughters,<ref name="census1891">{{cite web | title=1891 Census Swanage, Dorset, England RG12/1641 page 2 | url=https://www.ancestry.co.uk/imageviewer/collections/6598/images/DORRG12_1640_1643-0094?treeid=&personid=&rc=&usePUB=true&_phsrc=erq3884&_phstart=successSource&pId=16103596 |  access-date=16 September 2020}}</ref><ref name="Dr. W. L. Mollison." /> one of whom pre-deceased him.<ref name="Dr. W. L. Mollison." /><ref name="WWW" /> His wife died in 1917, and he provided the endowment for the [[Mayhew Prize]], a mathematics prize awarded by the University of Cambridge, in her honour.<ref name="WWW" /> His son, William Mayhew Mollison, was a distinguished ear, nose and throat surgeon,<ref>{{cite web |title=Mollison, William Mayhew (1878–1967) |url=https://livesonline.rcseng.ac.uk/client/en_GB/lives/search/detailnonmodal/ent:$002f$002fSD_ASSET$002f0$002f340476/one?qu=Mollison%2C+William+Mayhew&te=ASSET |website=Plarr's Lives of the Fellows |publisher=The Royal College of Surgeons of England |access-date=18 November 2018  |date=18 September 2014}}</ref> and his son [[Patrick Mollison]], a noted haematologist.<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Patrick Mollison |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/9023652/Professor-Patrick-Mollison.html |access-date=18 November 2018 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=18 January 2012}}</ref>

Mollison died on 10 March 1929 in London, England; he was aged 77.<ref name="obit Aberdeen" /><ref name="WWW" /> His funeral was held at the chapel of Clare College, Cambridge,<ref name="CAA" /> and he was buried in the [[Ascension Parish Burial Ground]] alongside his wife.<ref name="CAA" />
